titleEn: Even in the Dark, One Line of Light!

pages.text: "It's dark outside, Grandpa!" Coco looked up from the doorway. When the oven door closes and the alley lamps come on, it is bedtime. Grandpa Mole smiled, holding his bread. "A dark burrow is the coziest place."

In the loft, Coco pulled up the covers with just their nose showing. "Mom, can't I sleep with the lamp on?" "The bakery has to wake at dawn." Mom blew out the lamp. Everything went dark! Coco's heart thumped.
Faint light from an alley lamp came through the round window. On the wall—huh? A pointed shadow moved! To Coco, it looked just like a monster. Coco squeezed their eyes shut and hid under the covers.
"Sob, sob..." Mom heard and came quietly upstairs. She sat beside Coco with a little lamp and held their paw. Coco peeped out and pointed a paw at the wall. "There! A pointed monster!"
Mom raised the lamp toward the shadow. Light flashed across it. "Look! It's your headscarf on the peg!" The point was the scarf knot. Coco's mouth opened a little. "It was my scarf?"

This time Coco held the lamp. Light fell on a round shadow in the corner. "That's a flour sack!" Wherever the light shone, there were familiar things, no monsters. Coco's eyebrows lifted, and their mouth smiled.

Mom put out the lamp again. A thin line of light rose through a gap in the floor. "The oven fire glows all night. Its light comes up through the door gap," Mom whispered. "Even in the dark, one line of light! It's always here."
Now Coco wasn't afraid. "Dark just means the lamp is out!" Watching the line of light, Coco whispered, "Sleep tight, oven. Grandpa must be sleeping tight in his dark burrow too." Coco grinned.
When it grew dark, Coco did this. "One, say, 'I'm scared!' Two, shine the lamp on things one by one! Three, find the line of light on the floor!" Coco held Mom's paw tightly and nodded.

Night passed, and the kitchen was bright. Coco tightened the knot with both paws. Mom gave a snug hug. "Even when you're scared, a line of light is beside you." Coco called from her arms, "Even in the dark, one line of light!"
